title: PTZ Seizure Challenge: Assessment of Seizure Sensitivity in Mice
author: Sarah van Veen

steps.title: Prepare PTZ Injection
steps.instruction: Calculate the PTZ volume per animal based on body weight and prepare the solution in a syringe.

substeps.instruction: Calculate injection volume as 1% of body weight (10 mL/kg) to achieve a dose of 25 mg/kg.
Draw the PTZ solution into a 1 mL syringe equipped with a 27G needle.

steps.title: Administer PTZ
steps.instruction: Administer the PTZ solution to the mouse via intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection.

substeps.instruction: Inject PTZ i.p. at 1% body weight (25 mg/kg).
Note the exact time of injection.

steps.title: Initiate Observation and Recording
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in the observation environment and start data collection.

substeps.instruction: Immediately after injection, place the mouse in an observation box (15 x 15 cm, 30 cm high).
Simultaneously begin video recording and EthoVision XT tracking.

steps.title: Record and Score Behavior
steps.instruction: Continuously record and score seizure-related behaviors for 15 minutes, ensuring scoring is performed blind to genotype.

substeps.instruction: Score the occurrence and onset time of: (1) supine position (laying flat on floor), (2) head jerks, (3) Straub tail, (4) clonic seizures, and (5) tonic seizures.

steps.title: Monitor Humane Endpoints
steps.instruction: Observe animals throughout the procedure to ensure ethical standards.

substeps.instruction: If an animal reaches a humane endpoint (sustained generalized convulsions >60 s), intervene according to institutional ethics protocol.

steps.title: Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Process the recorded behavioral data to assess seizure susceptibility.

substeps.instruction: Record the occurrence and latency to onset for each scored behavior (supine position, head jerks, Straub tail, clonic seizures, and tonic seizures).
Compare occurrence and latency between WT and KO groups using appropriate non-parametric statistics (e.g., Mann-Whitney U) or survival analysis for latency to seizure onset.
